summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best performers are short, curious 'this thing doesn't see or hear the way you think' ideas about robots, clap switches and mics, and they also earn the most likes, saves and shares. Generic 'how does X work?' questions about everyday objects (taps, doors, smoke alarms, lifts) get weak results on both platforms, and a few videos were never posted to Instagram.
winningPattern: Robots and sound-based gadgets (gyro robot, clap switch, mic, line follower) with a bold, surprising claim as the hook, like 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y'. Titles are short Hinglish statements with one emoji, not a plain question. The winner is the Instagram Reel, with YouTube a smaller bonus. The gyro robot, clap switch and IR robot videos led on engagement (saves and shares), and the clap switch video got 1,269 IG views plus 598 on YouTube.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-style demos (balance, line following, obstacle avoidance) because they get the most views and saves
Open with a bold 'it doesn't X, it only Y' claim in the first line, in Hinglish
Make follow-ups to the clap switch and gyro robot, since viewers clearly want more of them
Post every video on both Instagram and YouTube; the PIR, Phone Up and Touchscreen videos got zero IG views because they were only posted on YouTube
Show the real hardware doing something visibly surprising in the first 2 seconds instead of just explaining
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' question titles on everyday objects like taps, lifts, mall doors and smoke detectors
Making several near-duplicate videos on the same topic (taps, smoke detectors, IR sensor) in a short time
Posting in English, since the one English video had very few views and no IG presence
